::: {}
### 10,000 files in 1.8 seconds

*Calepin* is written in Rust and renders complex markdown documents in under a millisecond. Smart caching means unchanged documents and code cost nothing.
:::

::: {}
### Instant preview

Run `calepin preview` to start a local server that watches your files and refreshes the browser on every save. Sub-millisecond renders mean the page updates before you can switch windows.
:::
:::

```bash
$ bench/gibberish.sh
10,000 files, 50 paragraphs each
5 sections x 3 subsections per file
prose + code + syntax highlighting + citations + cross-refs + footnotes + tables

1.780s total,  0.18ms/file
```


::: {.border-t .border-brd .mt-12 .pt-10}

### Extended Markdown

*Calepin* uses the [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) `.qmd` format: standard Markdown extended with executable code, structured content, and cross-referencing.

::: {.grid .grid-cols-1 .md:grid-cols-2 .gap-4 .mt-4 .text-sm}

::: {}
- R, Python, and Shell code chunks
- Inline code expressions
- Code chunk caching
- Figures, tables, and layouts
- Diagrams: TikZ, Mermaid, Graphviz, D2
:::

::: {}
- Citations and bibliography
- Cross-references and math
- Callout boxes and theorems
- Tabsets, fenced divs, and spans
- Syntax highlighting
- [And more...](pages/installation.html)
:::

:::
:::


::: {.border-t .border-brd .mt-12 .pt-10}

### Built for humans, with AI agents in mind

*Calepin* is designed so that LLM agents can read, understand, and modify every part of the system without special tooling. The file formats are ones that language models already know well: Markdown, HTML, Jinja, TOML.

There is no compiled CSS, no JavaScript build step, and no framework-specific class syntax to interpret. An agent that can read a plain HTML file can read a *Calepin* template.

Run `calepin extra skill` to install the *Calepin* "skill," then tell your agent what you need:

::: {.bg-code-bg .rounded-lg .p-4 .text-sm .italic .text-muted .border .border-brd}
/calepin Switch all the colors in my website to a muted pastel palette. Make the top navigation bar twice as wide. Align the footer text to the right. Remove the table of contents from the landing page but not the rest.
:::

::: {.grid .grid-cols-1 .md:grid-cols-3 .gap-6 .mt-8}

::: {.text-center}
::: {.font-mono .text-xs .font-bold .tracking-wider .text-faint .mb-1}
TAILWIND
:::
All styling via utility classes. Any Tailwind class works in fenced divs and spans.
:::

::: {.text-center}
::: {.font-mono .text-xs .font-bold .tracking-wider .text-faint .mb-1}
BUILD OPTIONAL
:::
No Node, no bundler, no compiled CSS pipeline to reproduce. Use external tools to optimize.
:::

::: {.text-center}
::: {.font-mono .text-xs .font-bold .tracking-wider .text-faint .mb-1}
PLAIN FORMATS
:::
Markdown, HTML, Jinja, TOML. Every format has broad LLM training coverage.
:::

:::

:::


::: {.border-t .border-brd .mt-12 .pt-10}

### Extensible

::: {.grid .grid-cols-1 .md:grid-cols-2 .gap-8}

::: {}
**Templates everywhere**

Every piece of output is a plain text template. Change how figures look, how code blocks render, how the navbar is laid out. Edit a simple text file to modify callouts, footnotes, the title block, or the entire page wrapper.
:::

::: {}
**Extensions in any language**

Write extensions in Python, R, bash, or any language you like. *Calepin* sends your script the document content, and your script sends back the modified version. Use what you know!
:::

:::
:::


::: {.border-t .border-brd .mt-12 .pt-10}

### Multiple output formats

The same `.qmd` source renders to HTML, LaTeX, Typst, and Markdown.

```
calepin notebook.qmd -t html
calepin notebook.qmd -t pdf
calepin notebook.qmd -t latex,typst

calepin init new_project -t website
calepin preview new_project
```
:::


::: {.callout-warning}
*Calepin* is alpha software. Please report bugs and feature requests at [github.com/vincentarelbundock/calepin](https://github.com/vincentarelbundock/calepin).

::: {.text-center .text-xs .text-faint .mt-12 .mb-4}
The name *Calepin* comes from the French word for a small pocket notebook.
:::
